mcqs.q: Fixed prosthodontics restores teeth with prostheses that are:
opts: Cemented or attached to the teeth and NOT removable by the patient
Removed and cleaned by the patient every night
Only used for children's primary teeth
Always made of acrylic and rest on the gums
mcqs.explain: Fixed prostheses are cemented (or implant-attached) and cannot be removed by the patient — unlike removable dentures.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a FIXED restoration?
mcqs.explain: A crown is a fixed (cemented) restoration; the others are removable appliances.

mcqs.q: A post & core is mainly used to:
opts: Rebuild a badly broken, root-canal-treated tooth so it can retain a crown
Replace an entire missing tooth in the arch
Cover only the biting surface of a molar
mcqs.explain: The post anchors in the root canal and the core rebuilds coronal structure to support a crown.

mcqs.q: A laminate veneer is best described as:
opts: A thin facing used mainly for anterior esthetics
A full-coverage metal restoration for molars
An artificial tooth suspended between two abutments
A titanium fixture placed into bone
mcqs.explain: Veneers are thin facings bonded to the front of (usually anterior) teeth for esthetics.

mcqs.q: A fixed dental prosthesis (bridge) is used to:
opts: Replace one or more missing teeth by cementing to prepared abutment teeth
Restore a single cavity within the cusps
mcqs.explain: A bridge replaces missing teeth and is cemented onto adjacent prepared abutments.

mcqs.q: A dental implant is:
opts: A titanium fixture placed in bone to support a crown
mcqs.explain: An implant is an osseointegrated titanium fixture that supports a crown/prosthesis.

mcqs.q: Which crown material generally gives the BEST esthetics?
mcqs.explain: All-ceramic crowns are the most esthetic; PFM balances esthetics and strength; metal is strongest but least esthetic.

mcqs.q: A porcelain-fused-to-metal (PFM) crown is chosen because it offers:
opts: A combination of esthetics and strength
No need for any tooth preparation
mcqs.explain: PFM combines a metal substructure (strength) with a porcelain veneer (esthetics).

mcqs.q: The main purpose of a provisional (temporary) crown is to:
opts: Protect the prepared tooth and maintain esthetics/function until the final crown
mcqs.explain: Provisionals protect the prepared tooth and preserve esthetics, function and tooth position between prep and cementation.

mcqs.q: In a fixed bridge, the artificial tooth that replaces the missing tooth is the:
mcqs.explain: Pontic = the artificial replacement tooth; it sits over the edentulous ridge.

mcqs.q: The prepared natural tooth that SUPPORTS a bridge is the:
mcqs.explain: The abutment is the prepared supporting tooth; the retainer is cemented onto it.

mcqs.q: The part of a bridge that joins the pontic to the retainer is the:
mcqs.explain: Connectors join the pontic to the retainers on either side.

mcqs.q: Extracoronal restorations are those that:
opts: Cover the external surface of the tooth (e.g. full or partial crowns)
Fit entirely within the tooth's anatomical contours
Are always removable by the patient
mcqs.explain: Extracoronal = covering the outside of the crown (full/partial veneer crowns).

mcqs.q: Intracoronal restorations are defined as those that:
opts: Fit within the anatomical contours of the clinical crown
Cover all external surfaces of the tooth
Are supported by a titanium implant
mcqs.explain: Intracoronal restorations (inlays/onlays) sit within the tooth's contours.

mcqs.q: The key difference between an onlay and an inlay is that an onlay:
opts: Covers one or more cusps, whereas an inlay does not
Is always made of gold, whereas an inlay is ceramic
Replaces a missing tooth, whereas an inlay does not
Is removable, whereas an inlay is fixed
mcqs.explain: An inlay lies between the cusps; an onlay additionally covers one or more cusps.

mcqs.q: The course carries a total of 6 credit hours, made up of:
mcqs.explain: Credit hours = 6 (2 lecture + 4 laboratory); contact hours 28 lecture + 112 lab = 140.

mcqs.q: To pass the course, a student must:
opts: Score ≥ 60% overall AND pass theory and practical separately
Score ≥ 60% overall only, regardless of components
mcqs.explain: ≥60% aggregate, plus ≥40% of the theory final and ≥50% aggregate of the practical — passed separately.

mcqs.q: Identify the labelled parts of this implant restoration (top → bottom):
mcqs.explain: From the visible crown down: crown (top) → abutment (middle) → implant fixture in bone (bottom).

mcqs.q: The course code for preclinical fixed prosthodontics is:
mcqs.explain: It is delivered in the 4th year of the BDS programme.

mcqs.q: The 6 credit hours of the course are made up of:
opts: 2 lectures + 4 laboratory hours — 28 lecture hours and 112 laboratory hours, 140 in total
mcqs.explain: The heavy laboratory weighting reflects that this is a preclinical skills course.

mcqs.q: The single-tooth preparation requirement of the laboratory course is:
mcqs.explain: Five three-unit bridges, six provisional crowns, five provisional bridges and two posts and cores are also required.

mcqs.q: Which is among the laboratory requirements of the course?
opts: Two diagnostic wax-ups and two wax patterns
mcqs.explain: Error-free alginate and final impressions, mounted diagnostic and master casts, and a custom tray are the others.

mcqs.q: Competency Test 2 assesses:
opts: A full-metal crown preparation on a posterior tooth, in Week 20
Evaluation of prepared teeth, in Week 9
An all-ceramic crown preparation on an anterior tooth, in Week 33
mcqs.explain: CT 1 is in Week 9, and CT 3 and CT 4 are both in Week 33.

mcqs.q: The theoretical half of the assessment (50 marks) is made up of:
mcqs.explain: The practical 50 marks comprise MPE 26, CBL 10 and CT 20.

mcqs.q: Under the special pass criteria, a student must obtain at least:
opts: 40% of the theory mark in the final (10) and 50% of the practical (25)
60% in the final written examination alone
50% of the theory mark and 40% of the practical
60% in each and every individual assessment
mcqs.explain: The general rule additionally requires a 60% aggregate across theory and practical together.

mcqs.q: Which textbook is listed as a reference for this course?
opts: Rosenstiel, Land & Fujimoto — Contemporary Fixed Prosthodontics, 6th ed.
Sturdevant — Art and Science of Operative Dentistry
mcqs.explain: Shillingburg's Fundamentals of Fixed Prosthodontics and Fundamentals of Tooth Preparation, and Rhoads' Dental Laboratory Procedures, are the others.

mcqs.q: The word 'fixed prosthodontics' breaks down as:
mcqs.explain: It is the branch concerned with restorations that are cemented and cannot be removed by the patient.

mcqs.q: A crown is defined as a restoration that:
opts: Covers or caps a prepared tooth to restore its shape, size, strength and appearance
Fits within the anatomical contours of the clinical crown
Replaces a missing tooth over an edentulous ridge
Is bonded to the facial surface of an anterior tooth
mcqs.explain: The last three describe an intracoronal restoration, a pontic and a laminate veneer.

mcqs.q: The three parts of a dental implant restoration, from bone outwards, are:
mcqs.explain: The titanium fixture placed in bone osseointegrates and replaces the tooth root.

mcqs.q: A FULL veneer (complete) crown is one that:
opts: Covers all surfaces of the clinical crown
Covers only some surfaces of the tooth
Restores the intracoronal area without covering cusps
Covers one or more cusps only
mcqs.explain: A partial coverage or partial veneer crown covers only some surfaces.

mcqs.q: Which learning outcome belongs to the SKILLS domain of this course?
opts: Perform tooth preparation for anterior and posterior teeth to receive a full veneer crown
List the instruments, materials and equipment used in fixed prosthodontics
Outline the safety measures required during the laboratory steps
Apply Islamic values and ethical principles in providing dental care
mcqs.explain: The first and third are knowledge outcomes; the last is a values outcome.

saqs.q: Define fixed prosthodontics and list the five main types of fixed restoration.
saqs.a: Fixed prosthodontics — restoring damaged teeth and replacing missing teeth with prostheses that are cemented or attached and NOT removable by the patient. Types: crown · post and core · laminate veneer · fixed dental prosthesis (bridge) · dental implant.

ans.text: The art and science of restoring damaged teeth and replacing missing teeth with prostheses that are cemented or attached and not removable by the patient.

saqs.q: Name the four parts of a fixed bridge and define each.
saqs.a: ABUTMENT — the prepared supporting tooth. RETAINER — the restoration cemented onto the abutment. PONTIC — the artificial tooth over the edentulous ridge. CONNECTOR — joins pontic to retainer.

head: Part
Definition
rows: the artificial tooth replacing the missing one, over the edentulous ridge

saqs.q: Differentiate extracoronal from intracoronal restorations, giving an example of each.
saqs.a: EXTRACORONAL — covers the external surface (full-veneer/complete crown, partial-veneer crown). INTRACORONAL — fits within the anatomical contours of the clinical crown (inlay, onlay).

head: EXTRACORONAL
INTRACORONAL
rows: covers the external surface of the tooth
fits within the anatomical contours of the clinical crown

saqs.q: Differentiate an inlay from an onlay.
saqs.a: An INLAY restores a cavity lying between the cusps and does NOT cover a cusp. An ONLAY is similar but additionally COVERS one or more cusps.

head: INLAY
ONLAY
rows: restores a cavity between the cusps — does not cover a cusp
the same, but additionally covers one or more cusps

saqs.q: List three crown materials with one property of each, and state the purpose of a provisional crown.
saqs.a: ALL-CERAMIC — best esthetics. PFM — esthetics plus strength. METAL (gold) — maximum strength with least tooth reduction. A PROVISIONAL crown protects the prepared tooth and maintains esthetics, function and tooth position until the final crown is cemented.

ans.text: Also all-resin and stainless-steel. A provisional crown protects the prepared tooth and maintains esthetics, function and tooth position until the final crown is cemented.

saqs.q: Outline the assessment structure and pass criteria of the course.
saqs.a: 100 marks: THEORETICAL 50 (ESE1 15, MSE2 10, Final 25) + PRACTICAL 50 (MPE 26, CBL 10, CT 20). GENERAL — 60% aggregate across theory and practical together. SPECIAL — theory and practical must pass separately: ≥40% of the theory mark in the final (10) and ≥50% aggregate of the practical (25).

head: Rule
Requirement
rows: an aggregate of 60% across theory and practical/clinical together
theory and practical must also pass separately — at least 40% of the theory mark in the final exam (10 marks), and at least 50% aggregate of the practical marks (25 marks)

saqs.q: List the laboratory requirements and the four competency tests of the course.
saqs.a: LAB — 10 single-tooth preparations (6 posterior, 4 anterior) · 5 three-unit bridges · 6 provisional crowns · 5 provisional bridges · 2 posts and cores · error-free alginate and final impressions · mounted diagnostic and master casts · a custom tray · 2 diagnostic wax-ups · 2 wax patterns. CT 1 prepared teeth (Wk 9) · CT 2 full-metal crown, posterior (Wk 20) · CT 3 all-ceramic, anterior (Wk 33) · CT 4 provisional crown (Wk 33).
